public_rationale: The study available on May 14, 2024 reports prompt refinement over three iterations using GPT-4V feedback with DALL-E 3 [e4]. It tests a custom automated workflow on attribute and relation prompts and reference-image recreation [e4]. These results do not establish whether ordinary ChatGPT successfully applied the claimed November 2024 corrections to image parts [e4].
limitations: The original November 2024 before-and-after images were not independently verified.
The packet contains no comparable November test of part-specific feedback in ordinary ChatGPT.
Success in a custom automated workflow does not contradict a claim of difficulty in ordinary interaction.
The evidence does not establish an internal cause of correction failures.

statement.document_title: Don’t Ride This Bike! Generative AI’s persistent trouble with compositionality and parts

from_speaker: associating user feedback with parts of images
our_interpretation: The plain reading is behavioral: the system repeatedly fails to apply clear corrections about particular image parts. It does not establish a specific internal cognitive mechanism.
The three examples are bicycle labels, rabbit ears, and the violin bridge.
The target period is November 2024, when the post says these interactions occurred.
Difficulty permits occasional successful corrections; it does not mean feedback never helps.
criteria.support_condition: Verified interaction sequences show that clear feedback about the relevant parts is followed by images retaining the specified errors across the three examples or closely comparable repeated tests.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The complete interaction records show that the specified corrections were successfully applied, or directly comparable testing establishes that the apparent failures resulted from misdescription or scoring errors.
